run.question: My AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 has high latency issues. Investigate why.

report.summary: No AWS Lambda function named 'payment-processor' and no us-east-1 Lambda data are present in or available to this target. The target is a kind cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane) running the OpenTelemetry demo in namespace otel-demo; the only payment entity is Deployment/Service/Pod 'payment' (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment). I found no Lambda, aws or CloudWatch object, no CloudWatch data source among the available integrations, and no trace/metric data at all (every Prometheus and Jaeger call in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so the reported high latency could not be measured and no latency trend or baseline exists. What could be checked looks healthy rather than slow: all 21 otel-demo deployments report 1/1 ready and available, the payment pod is Running and ready, and payment's own application log shows charge requests completed in about 1-2 ms with no error lines; in checkout's log the PlaceOrder -> 'payment went through' step took roughly 13-23 ms for the six sampled orders. One change inside the window remains unexplained: every pod in otel-demo and kube-system terminated with exit code 255 reason 'Unknown' at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z and static control-plane pods were recreated at 04:23:46Z, consistent with a node/runtime restart; its trigger is not established, and all pods are Running again. Because the named function does not exist in this environment and no latency metric could be read, the question about 'payment-processor' high latency is unresolved (partial/inconclusive on cause); root cause is not asserted.

claims.text: A cluster-wide query of Deployments returned 24 objects, all in kube-system, local-path-storage or otel-demo, with images such as registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.14.6 and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment; it contained no 'payment-processor' workload and no Lambda/aws image.

A cluster-wide query of Services returned 29 services; the payment-related identity is Service 'payment' in namespace otel-demo on port 8080 (plus Service 'prometheus-readonly-proxy' on 9090). No service named 'payment-processor' appeared in the returned list.
In namespace otel-demo all 21 Deployments reported ready=1, available=1, updated=1 and spec.replicas=1, including 'payment'; no deployment was short of replicas at query time.

Deployment 'payment' (namespace otel-demo) runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment with env PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013 and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317, and a memory limit of 120Mi.

Pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (namespace otel-demo) is Running with its container ready, restartCount 1, and last termination exitCode 255 with reason 'Unknown' finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z; there is no OOMKilled reason on it.

The payment container's own log shows successful charges with no error lines: 194 lines were read between 06:43:25.222Z and 06:58:59.999Z, and each 'Charge request received.' is followed by 'Transaction complete.' within about 1-2 ms (e.g. 2026-11-21T06:43:25.222819459Z -> 06:43:25.224041507Z, and 06:58:59.997856290Z -> 06:58:59.999394934Z).

ConfigMap flagd-config (namespace otel-demo) declares every feature flag with defaultVariant 'off', including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), cartFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage; the only delay-shaped flag is imageSlowLoad ('slow loading images in the frontend', variants 10sec/5sec/off), also defaultVariant 'off'.

Every one of the 22 otel-demo pods shows restartCount >= 1 with last termination exitCode 255 / reason 'Unknown' finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, with two exceptions: kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz (restarts 2, last termination exitCode 1 reason 'Error' finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:24:17Z) and prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (restarts 3, last termination exitCode 1 reason 'Error' startedAt 2026-11-21T04:24:05Z, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z).

The same termination appears cluster-wide in kube-system: coredns-559f6c778d-bwl2n, coredns-559f6c778d-lfqlc, kindnet-h8zr5, kube-proxy-s9mt7, kube-controller-manager-opspilot-m1-control-plane and kube-scheduler-opspilot-m1-control-plane each show last termination exitCode 255 reason 'Unknown' finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, while etcd-opspilot-m1-control-plane and kube-apiserver-opspilot-m1-control-plane were created at 2026-11-21T04:23:46Z.
Node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False at query time.
Cluster-wide queries returned zero NetworkPolicy objects and zero ResourceQuota objects.

Payment's own application log shows no error lines and charge handling completing in about 1-2 ms per request across 06:43-06:59, which does not support a payment-side processing slowdown in that sampled interval (it is a log sample, not a latency measurement).

All otel-demo Deployments, including payment, held their full 1/1 ready and available replica counts and the payment pod was Running and ready, so no pod-level unavailability or image/rollout problem is visible for the payment workload.

The reported entity 'AWS Lambda payment-processor in us-east-1' is not part of this target; the nearest analogous entity is Deployment/Service/Pod 'payment' in namespace otel-demo (OpenTelemetry demo), so latency evidence gathered here cannot be attributed to the named Lambda function.

The unavailability of every Prometheus and Jaeger query in this Run may be related to the prometheus-readonly-proxy pod (nginx, upstream Prometheus on 9090) which has 3 restarts and last termination exitCode 1 reason 'Error' at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z; this is unverified because its nginx configuration lives in a Secret that cannot be read and its containers returned no log lines.

The cluster-wide termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (every pod, exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', followed by static control-plane pods recreated at 04:23:46Z) is more consistent with a node/kubelet or container-runtime restart than with an application fault in payment, but nothing observed ties it to the reported latency and its trigger is unknown.

Fault injection through the demo feature flags was considered and rejected as an explanation for payment latency: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config, including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, has defaultVariant 'off', and no flag targeting payment introduces a delay (the only delay flag, imageSlowLoad, affects frontend image loading).

Pod eviction, OOMKill or resource-quota exhaustion was considered and rejected as an explanation for payment trouble: the payment pod shows no OOMKilled termination reason, no Evicted/backoff state, and cluster-wide queries returned zero ResourceQuota objects.

Re-run the latency investigation against an AWS-integrated target (CloudWatch Lambda Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions and CloudWatch Logs per the 'lambda-performance-troubleshooting' runbook) or provide a CloudWatch data source; those steps could not be executed here because no CloudWatch/AWS tool exists in this Run's available data sources.

Restore the metrics/traces query path (investigate the prometheus-readonly-proxy restarts with exit code 1 and the Prometheus/Jaeger endpoint reachability) before drawing any latency conclusion about the payment service in otel-demo.

gaps: No entity named 'payment-processor' exists in this target: the returned inventories of Deployments (24 objects) and Services (29 objects) contain no such name, and no AWS Lambda/CloudWatch source is among the available data sources (available: jaeger, kubernetes, prometheus, knowledge; not_integrated: change_history), so Lambda Duration/InitDuration/ConcurrentExecutions and CloudWatch Logs could not be checked at all.

Every Prometheus call in this Run (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_prometheus_target) and every Jaeger call (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags) returned status error / reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no latency series, error-rate reading or span duration was obtained; latency, its trend and any comparable baseline for the payment service are unknown rather than zero.

A cluster-wide Events query returned zero events inside the authorized window (view status no_data), so Evicted, OOMKilled, FailedScheduling, Unhealthy or rollout event evidence is unknown, not absent.

The cause of the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z cluster-wide container termination (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown') and of the control-plane pod recreation at 04:23:46Z is not established; no node conditions or events record it.
Runtime feature-flag state in flagd is not readable: only the ConfigMap defaultVariant values ('off') were seen, so whether any flag was enabled at evaluation time is unknown.

prometheus-readonly-proxy's nginx configuration is stored in a Secret that cannot be read, its containers returned zero log lines on both current and previous instance, and the reason for its three exit-code-1 terminations is unverified.

The payment service has no own latency measurement in the available evidence: the 1-2 ms charge completion and 13-23 ms checkout PlaceOrder-to-payment intervals are log-timestamp observations on a low-volume sample (~97 charges in the sampled 15.5 minutes), not a response-time distribution.
next_steps: Ask for the AWS account/region (us-east-1) Lambda telemetry to be onboarded as a data source so CloudWatch Duration, InitDuration and ConcurrentExecutions for function 'payment-processor' can be queried over this same window.

If the intent is the Kubernetes payment service, restore Prometheus/Jaeger reachability (check prometheus-readonly-proxy restarts and its Secret-backed nginx config, and the exporter scrape targets) and then compare p50/p95/p99 of rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket for payment and its callers before and after 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z.
Confirm whether the node/runtime restart at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z was planned (node maintenance/upgrade) and, if so, exclude it before comparing latency baselines.

content.name: lambda-performance-troubleshooting
content.content:
# AWS Lambda High Latency Troubleshooting

## Overview
This runbook helps diagnose and resolve AWS Lambda function performance issues including high latency, timeouts, and cold starts.

## Steps

### Step 1: Query Performance Metrics
Use CloudWatch to check Lambda function latency over time:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name Duration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 2: Check Function Logs
Look for errors or slow operations in CloudWatch Logs:
```bash
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --filter-pattern "[ERROR] OR [WARN] OR timeout" --limit 100
```

### Step 3: Analyze Cold Start Patterns
Query CloudWatch for cold start frequency:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name InitDuration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Count --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 4: Check Concurrent Executions
Verify Lambda isn't hitting concurrency limits:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name ConcurrentExecutions --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 60
```

### Step 5: Review Memory Utilization
Check if function needs more memory allocation:
```bash
aws logs insights start-query --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --start-time <epoch-start> --end-time <epoch-end> \
  --query-string "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @type = 'REPORT' | stats max(@maxMemoryUsed), avg(@memorySize)"
```
